html:
Ordu-Baliq, also called Karabalgasun, was the capital of the Uyghur Khaganate in the Orkhon valley of Mongolia, from the 740s until it was sacked in 840.

The Uyghurs built it as a walled city with a palace, temples, markets and farms, rare on the steppe. It grew rich from trade with Tang China, which paid in silk for horses and military help after the An Lushan revolt. Arab travellers described its gates and crowded streets. Its rulers took up Manichaeism, and a three-language inscription stood there.

In 840 the Yenisei Kyrgyz from the north sacked the city and broke the khaganate. The Uyghurs fled south into the Tarim Basin and Gansu, where their heirs live today. Four centuries later the Mongols built Karakorum nearby.
sum: Ordu-Baliq, also called Karabalgasun, was the capital of the Uyghur Khaganate in the Orkhon valley of Mongolia, from the 740s until it was sacked in 840.
